entries.name: Sam Day

expected_cases.charges: Federal trespass and related — multiple anti-nuclear civil disobedience actions
expected_cases.sentence: Cumulative federal time across multiple sentences

expected_cases.charges: Violation of Army regulation prohibiting demonstrations at Fort McCoy — January 17, 1991 antiwar leafleting
expected_cases.sentence: Four-month sentence for the January 17, 1991 Fort McCoy antiwar action. Day described remaining in Rock County Jail after arrest, then transfer to Dane County Jail following the March 26 verdict. His later first-person account identifies May 13, 1991 as his first day free after completing the term at Rock County Jail. The April 24 sentencing date was prospective in the earlier article and is not entered as a confirmed date. This interval does not include his other anti-nuclear protest cases.

case.charges: Unlawful re-entry at Offutt Air Force Base — February 1995 anti-nuclear leafleting
case.sentence: Six-month federal misdemeanor sentence for unlawful re-entry at Offutt Air Force Base. The Witness (May 1995, p. 21) reports continuous jail custody from the February 20 protest. Day describes the first two months in county jail and the remainder at Oxford Federal Prison Camp; the Fall 1995 Nukewatch Pathfinder (p. 6) confirms his August 18 release. These endpoints establish 179 elapsed days; the announced 180-day sentence is not used as an actual time-served total. This is separate from his 1991 Fort McCoy imprisonment.

entries.name: Michele Naar-Obed

expected_cases.charges: Trespass / destruction of government property (Plowshares direct action)
expected_cases.sentence: On August 6, 1995 (Hiroshima Day), as part of the Jubilee Plowshares/East action, Naar-Obed and partners entered Newport News Shipbuilding and boarded the USS Greenville in dry dock, pouring blood and hammering areas associated with cruise-missile capability. Arrested and prosecuted; received 12 months in federal prison. Her probation was later revoked and she was returned to federal custody in July 1999.

case.charges: Supervision violation — returning to Jonah House following the Jubilee Plowshares East case
case.sentence: One-year term after revocation of supervision for returning to Jonah House. The September-October 1999 Earth First! roster reports return to prison in July 1999 at Western Tidewater Regional Jail. The Plowshares Disarmament Chronology, 1980-2003 (p. 58) reports actual release on June 21, 2000. Admission is known only to the month; no exact day or twelve-month actual time-served total is inferred. This is a separate custody episode from the 1995 action and its initial sentence.

sources: Arthur J. Laffin, The Plowshares Disarmament Chronology, 1980-2003, printed page 58 (user-supplied PDF page 70).
